invariants: export acceptance commits the frozen query, idempotency result, minimum audit and requested outbox in one PostgreSQL transaction
the worker reads a deterministic tenant-scoped PostgreSQL snapshot and never relies on the browser page currently in memory
a completed job points to a MinIO object through a PostgreSQL manifest containing sha256, size, MIME type, retention and business reference
requested and completed lifecycle events use a leased PostgreSQL outbox; broker acknowledgement precedes published state, transient failure is retried and exhausted delivery is retained as dead
download verifies tenant, lifecycle, retention, object size and sha256 and commits an audit record before serving bytes
column preferences are tenant-and-user scoped and require optimistic revision on every update
domain.compensation: disable API and worker; retain jobs, audit, manifests and objects for reconciliation; deterministic object keys make retries overwrite-safe

negative_tests: viewer cannot create, read or download exports without asset:export
cross-tenant job and object access returns no resource
a user cannot read or overwrite another user's column preference

stop_conditions: row or byte cap exceeded, object manifest mismatch, PostgreSQL queue latency or worker resource usage exceeds the approved budget

tests: G0 OpenAPI, feature contract, generated client and migration lint
G1 validation, scope, idempotency, rendering and optimistic revision tests
G2 real PostgreSQL transaction, Kafka broker acknowledgement and MinIO object-store worker
G3 job, audit, leased outbox, consumed Kafka event, manifest, object and preference reconciliation
G4 fixed-scale export and download resource budget
G5 Windows Chrome submit-progress-download and column-settings journey
evidence: same trace_id across 202 response, job, audit, outbox and object manifest; browser artifact sha256 equals PostgreSQL manifest and served header
